question.text: Ms. Riya, HNI investor (Rs. 100 crore portfolio), currently has 25% in domestic small-cap stocks and a self-imposed maximum exposure cap of 40% to small-caps. She's considering Cat III AIF 'A' (long-short small-cap). Her BEST action:

answer.text: Allocate the full Rs. 20 crore being raised to Fund A
Limit allocation to Fund A to a maximum of Rs. 15 crore so total small-cap exposure stays within the 40% cap, and consider Fund B for the balance to diversify

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook example takes a Rs. 100 crore portfolio that already has 25% (Rs. 25 crore) in domestic small-cap stocks, with the investor's own cap at 40% (Rs. 40 crore). That leaves headroom of Rs. 15 crore for an additional small-cap-only allocation such as Fund A. The remaining commitment should go to a different style — such as a market-neutral Fund B — so the small-cap cap is respected while still deploying capital across managers. The Trap: Allocating the full Rs. 20 crore to Fund A would breach the 40% small-cap cap. Exiting small-cap entirely abandons an existing strategic allocation, and doubling small-cap exposure ignores the cap altogether. Note: The Rs. 100 crore portfolio with 25% existing small-cap, 40% cap, and Rs. 15 crore maximum allocation to a small-cap-only fund is taken from the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B).
